newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - Czech insurer sees loss after bank fails.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Czech insurer sees loss after bank fails.

text.p: Losses from the failed Kreditni Banka a.s. forced Czech insurer, Ceska Pojistovna a.s., on Thursday to cut its net 1996 earnings forecast to a loss from its original projection of 470 million Czech crowns ($17.73 million) in net profit.

Company officials said on Thursday that Pojistovna should be able to cover the 5.9 billion crowns in its liabilities in the bank through its reserves augmented by a 1.14 billion crown rights issue and 1996 revenues.
Still, Pojistovna board member Ladislav Bartonicek told a news conference after an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) that the insurance company might post a net loss for the year.
"It should not be a dramatically negative number," he said.
Pojistovna was stung by last month's collapse of the medium-sized Plzen-based Kreditni Banka in which it holds a 66 percent stake.
The insurer on Thursday declared a loss of its 1.5 billion crowns in basic equity in Kreditni and another 4.7 billion crowns in deposits with the bank.
Some of the deposits would be covered by the liquidation of Kreditni's assets.
In June, the Czech National Bank (CNB) on advice from independent auditors directed Kreditni to build reserves against losses of 11.8 billion crowns, Pojistovna said.
The CNB cancelled Kreditni's banking licence at the beginning of August declaring it insolvent.
Local analysts have blamed Kreditni's failure on dubious loans made by banking management to interests connected to shareholders, and the issue has become a political football.
The Czech cabinet on Wednesday assigned three ministers to lead a criminal investigation into the bank's collapse.
Bartonicek said Pojistovna had filed a criminal complaint against an unknown offender in the Kreditni case, but he declined to elaborate.
The Kreditni case has shaken the management of Pojistovna just as large stakes in the company have been changing hands.
Bartonicek said former chairman Vlastimil Uzel, removed from head of the board earlier this year, had also resigned as general director, taking up a post as deputy director.

Pojistovna revealed on Thursday that the Czech financial group PPF had become its largest shareholder with a 36 percent stake after acquiring a 16 percent stake from Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB).

Bartonicek, who represents PPF on Pojistovna's board, said PPF had options to buy another seven percent stake in the insurer from Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., and had an interest in taking CSOB's remaining seven percent.
If those acquisitions are completed, PPF would have majority control of Pojistovna.
Market analysts had suspected that PPF had acquired IPB's stake, but with opaque Czech disclosure rules, the acquisition was not made public until Thursday.
IPB still legally held its shares in Pojistovna at the August 28 cutoff date for the rights issue, approved by the meeting on Thursday, and will assign the new shares to PPF.

The new shares with a nominal value of 1,000 crowns will be offered at 5,000 crowns with the premium going to partially cover Kreditni losses. Pojistovna's shares fell 200 crowns on Thursday on the Prague Stock Exchange to 3,800.
Bartonicek said that the issue is expected to be fully subscribed by current shareholders which include the state National Property Fund and Komercni Banka a.s..
-- Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003 ($1=26.51 Czech Crown)
